WHAT WAS REFUTED, and it is the reason this function was nearly lost: PL measured the regnorm POSITIONAL map as INCONSISTENT on every callee-saved register (r26->r30x13/r26x1, r27->r30x2/r29x1/r27x1, r28->r27x2/r28x2, r29->r28x5/r26x3/r29x1, r30->r29x8/r30x1), read that as the web-split tell, and wrote that the function is 'NOT a copy_register_fields candidate without a def-site-grouped audit ... recorded so a later lane does not mistake CLEAN-RENAMING alone for WebFrank eligibility'. Measured through the shipped apply_patch, copy_register_fields alone closes it to residual 0. The inference does not hold because the two tools compute different things: regnorm pairs POSITIONALLY and reports ONE whole-function map, so a register that legitimately carries two different values in two DISJOINT live ranges reads as inconsistent; verify_consistent_recolor adjudicates the renaming along DEF-USE WEBS, where those same two live ranges are separate bindings and no conflict exists. A positional-map inconsistency is therefore evidence about regnorm's pairing model, not about WebFrank eligibility. SOURCE-EXHAUSTION PROVENANCE remains PL's record, whose two literal probed_form axes (reassociating the pot+prod call argument, extending the opt_common_subs bracket) were both kept and drove the residual to an identical 80/80 multiset with 0 ops clusters.
